## Explore the weather data

Choose a city and measure from the menu inside the chart. The date-range slider lets you focus on a particular part of 2019–2025. The readings are hourly observations, so zooming in reveals changes across individual hours rather than daily averages.

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go

# Load 10-year hourly weather dataset starting from 2019
weather_data = pd.read_csv("hourly_temperatures.csv")
weather_data["date"] = pd.to_datetime(weather_data["date"])
weather_data = weather_data[weather_data["date"].dt.year >= 2019].dropna(subset=["temp_f"]).copy()
weather_data = weather_data.rename(columns={"rainfall_mm": "prcp"})

fig = go.Figure()
selections = [
    ("Sarasota", "Temperature", "temp_f", "Temperature (°F)", "#1C6E8C"),
    ("Sarasota", "Rainfall", "prcp", "Rainfall (mm)", "#D96C06"),
    ("Ulaanbaatar", "Temperature", "temp_f", "Temperature (°F)", "#1C6E8C"),
    ("Ulaanbaatar", "Rainfall", "prcp", "Rainfall (mm)", "#D96C06"),
]

for city, measure, column, y_title, color in selections:
    city_data = weather_data[weather_data["city"] == city]
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=city_data["date"],
            y=city_data[column],
            mode="lines",
            line={"color": color, "width": 1},
            name=f"{city} {measure}",
            visible=(city == "Sarasota" and measure == "Temperature"),
            hovertemplate="%{x|%b %d, %H:%M}<br>%{y:.1f}<extra></extra>",
        )
    )

buttons = []
for index, (city, measure, column, y_title, color) in enumerate(selections):
    visible = [False] * len(selections)
    visible[index] = True
    buttons.append(
        {
            "label": f"{city}: {measure}",
            "method": "update",
            "args": [
                {"visible": visible},
                {
                    "title.text": f"{city} hourly {measure.lower()} readings in 2019–2025",
                    "yaxis.title.text": y_title,
                },
            ],
        }
    )

fig.update_layout(
    template="plotly_white",
    title=dict(
        text="Sarasota hourly temperature readings in 2019–2025",
        x=0.5,
        xanchor="center",
        y=0.97,
        yanchor="top",
    ),
    height=600,
    hovermode="x unified",
    xaxis={
        "title": "Date and time",
        "rangeslider": {"visible": True},
        "rangeselector": {
            "buttons": [
                {"count": 1, "label": "1 month", "step": "month", "stepmode": "backward"},
                {"count": 3, "label": "3 months", "step": "month", "stepmode": "backward"},
                {"count": 1, "label": "1 year", "step": "year", "stepmode": "backward"},
                {"step": "all", "label": "All available"},
            ],
            "x": 0,
            "xanchor": "left",
            "y": 1.12,
            "yanchor": "top",
        },
    },
    yaxis={"title": "Temperature (°F)"},
    updatemenus=[
        {
            "type": "buttons",
            "direction": "left",
            "buttons": buttons,
            "showactive": True,
            "x": 0.5,
            "xanchor": "center",
            "y": 1.28,
            "yanchor": "top",
            "pad": {"r": 4, "t": 4},
        }
    ],
    margin={"t": 160, "r": 30, "b": 80, "l": 70},
)
fig.show()
```

Use the menu to compare the two cities and switch between temperature and rainfall. Try narrowing the slider to winter or summer to see when the two places differ most across 2019–2025.
